findings.reason: §16's stated compatibility mechanism is insufficient for records written between §14 and §16, so the section must add the intermediate form or restate the coverage rule.
findings.text: `_fingerprint_forms` returns exactly `{plan_fingerprint(content), plan_fingerprint(content, legacy=True)}`; §16 redefines the default `plan_fingerprint` to the digest of a sorted per-section set, so after §16 a record stored under the current (post-landing-collapse) whole-document digest matches neither the new current form nor the pre-collapse legacy form and earns a fresh review — the re-review wave §14's correction (eleven stored sidecars flipping) and §16 itself exist to prevent; §16 should retain the pre-§16 current digest as an additional recognised form, or narrow its claim that "a record stored before this change ... still satisfies the gate"

findings.reason: the finding names the file to extend, and §16 must cite and resolve the workspace/structure layer (hoist the enumerator into reckon/_store.py) rather than implying a new walker.
findings.text: `_authored_section_headings` already returns a plan's authored `(identity, heading)` pairs in document order, handling the h2-id and wrapper-id cases, which is the enumeration §16's per-section walk needs; §16 names only `reckon/_store.py`'s `_section_heading`/`landed_section_ids` (single-id extent and a landed-id set, neither of which enumerates), so the walk would become a third section segmenter beside _store.py and mcp_views.py

findings.reason: §2 is already landed at impl 0.6, so stating its interface accounting now edits documentation of shipped work rather than changing what is built; §16, the pending node, already complies.
findings.text: §2's own text adds a subsystem's surface — the review store module, the `crew review-plan` command with its options, the `plan-review` crew view and the `plan-review-missing` refusal family — and names none of it as retired, merged, or impossible to retire, the one rule §3 itself imposes on sections; §16 by contrast satisfies the rule in its own text

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — reckon/crew/plan_review.py (994 lines) hides the record shape, the store, the version-keyed path, the fingerprint join and the response bookkeeping behind the public functions, and §16 adds the per-section coverage question to that same owner rather than to a new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 proposes a per-section authored walk but cites no existing enumerator; `reckon/mcp_views.py:2080 _authored_section_headings` already enumerates a plan's authored sections in document order and should be the owner extended (or hoisted into reckon/_store.py) rather than a third walker accreting in plan_review.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 accounts for its own surface (one new public definition, no new refusal family), but §2 adds the review store, the `crew review-plan` options (reckon/cli.py:2579), the `plan-review` MCP view (reckon/mcp.py:4301) and the `plan-review-missing` refusal family (reckon/cli.py:2119) with no in-text statement of what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanisms it extends, naming the build skill's reuse-map rule (skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:91) that §3 turns into a review and the code-review reflex that §2's store and §16's fingerprint reuse (reckon/crew/recovery.py:520 `_review_dispatch_fields` dispatches both a run subject and a plan subject through one composer).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §16's compatibility story reuses `_fingerprint_forms` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598), which carries only two digests, so it cannot keep a record stored under the current pre-§16 definition current once §16 redefines the current digest.
